newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indexes quiet as market moves up.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indexes quiet as market moves up.

text.p: Major U.S. index options trading was on the light side Friday, with one trader saying the market was "going up on air."
Traders noted that activity in stock index futures was also relatively quiet.
"Trading has been very, very light. Futures have been very, very thin," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in S&P 100 index .OEX options.
An S&P 500 index .SPX futures-options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said that even when futures trading popped, the options remained quiet.
"The last (intraday) rally brought business to S&Ps but not the options," he said. "The options are real quiet."
In early afternoon, September S&P 500 futures were up six points at 927.50. The spot SPX index gained 5.68 to 919.46 and the OEX added 6.29 to 896.51.
The bellwether Dow industrial average .DJI rose 67 points to 7,954.
Callahan said that despite the sluggish pace of trading, the bias was on the buy side.
"A market like this could run," the futures-options trader said, noting that once bonds close, stocks could move sharply.
One options dealer in Chicago said that although the market had upside potential, some investors were growing cautious.
"People are a little more leery when you hit the big numbers," he said, citing 8,000 on the Dow.
"So there's been a little bit of hesitancy to buy right here, a little bit of profit-taking."
He added that index put buying picked up earlier in the week as the Dow neared the 8,000 mark.
"I don't think those people (put buyers) got satisfied even though the market dropped because the puts didn't really go anywhere," the dealer said.
On Wednesday, the Dow reached 7,991 before backing off to close more than 100 points lower.
Traders said major index volatilities were flat to slightly lower, with time decay eroding premiums ahead of the weekend. In addition, the July options expire next week.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange's volatility index .VIX was down 0.05 at 22.36. It is derived off certain OEX contracts.
